# Quantitative contact-certificate rigidity and optimized-parameter continuity

This note proves quantitative stability of the contributor's global parameter certificate,
then continuity of optimized parameters under actual positive-fiber body
perturbations. No regular cap, differentiable optimizer, affine center selector,
or identification of the volume and surface martingales is assumed.

The topology in the conclusion is important: uniform convergence on compact
fiber interiors, mixed L1 and logarithmic L1 convergence, and uniform convergence
of the actual energy-weighted buffers. Uniform convergence of the parameters at
sampled fiber boundaries is not claimed. Nor is uniqueness or convergence of an
arbitrary extension between sampled fibers asserted.

Dependencies are the contact certificate and its proper-source strictness in
`candidate b2578378c7102b3c`,
the joint marked-energy continuity and all-direction slab comparison in
`candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`, and the elementary
concave-function logarithmic bounds reproved below. The present result is
conditional on a limiting certificate; it supplies no new Gamma payment or
body-minimum existence theorem.

## 1. Actual fixed-body certificate

Let P be a finite base, with positive full-dimensional d-fibers K_z, d>=1,
and actual compatible canonical hull C=conv union_z({z} x K_z). Write

    S=union_z({z} x K_z),  dm=sum_z dX|K_z,
    V_z=|K_z|,  M=sum_z V_z,  dP_0=dm/M,  N=d+1.

Relative ambient geometry is taken in aff(P) x R^d. Let L be positive,
continuous and concave on C, with E_(P_0) log L=0. Suppose there are marks
Y_i=(p_i,y_i), positive weights sigma_i summing to one, and probability rows
rho_i, such that, with L_i=L(Y_i),

    E_(rho_i) w=Y_i,
    E_(rho_i) L=L_i,
    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) rho_i=dm/(M L).                 (1)

These are actual full-space barycenters. In particular each rho_i is supported
on S, and gives no mass to the relative boundaries of its sampled fibers:
its positive multiple is dominated by the absolutely continuous target in (1).

For any positive continuous concave U on C, put R=U/L. Jensen row by row gives

    b:=E_(P_0) R
       =sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) E_(rho_i) U
       <=sum_i sigma_i U(Y_i)/L_i.                    (2)

No row is required to be uniform or to be supported on one fiber.

## 2. Quantitative entropy and L1 rigidity

Assume also E_(P_0) log U=0 and

    U(Y_i)/L_i <= exp(delta) for every i,  delta>=0.   (3)

Then Jensen for log, followed by (2), gives

    1<=b<=exp(delta).

The probability measure Q_R=(R/b)P_0 satisfies the exact identity

    KL(P_0 || Q_R)=log b-E_(P_0)log R=log b<=delta.    (4)

Pinsker's inequality in the convention ||mu-nu||_1<=sqrt(2 KL(mu||nu))
therefore gives

    E_(P_0)|R-1|
      <=exp(delta)sqrt(2 delta)+exp(delta)-1
      =:omega(delta).                                (5)

Consequently

    integral_S |U-L| dm <= M L_max omega(delta),      (6)

where L_max=max_S L. In particular delta=0 recovers exact sampled rigidity.
Only the original mixed measure occurs; there is no replacement of the integer
sum by an integral over the base hull.

For completeness, the Pinsker form used here follows by splitting into
A={dmu>=dnu}, applying the log-sum inequality to A and its complement, and
using the two-point bound KL((p,1-p)||(q,1-q))>=2(p-q)^2. The latter follows
by differentiating in p: the second derivative is 1/[p(1-p)]>=4, with value
and first derivative zero at p=q. Thus no unproved transport estimate enters
(5).

## 3. From L1 to uniform convergence on fiber interiors

Two elementary quantitative facts suffice. For a nonnegative concave function
v on a full-dimensional convex body K, let m=max_K v. Homothety about a
maximizer shows

    |{v>=t m}| >= (1-t)^d |K|,  0<=t<=1,
    m <= (d+1)|K|^(-1) integral_K v.                  (7)

The first statement uses v((1-t)x+t x_max)>=t m for x in K. Integration
in t proves the second. Applied to U and (2), it gives

    max_(K_z) U <= (d+1) M L_max exp(delta)/V_z.       (8)

Fix rho>0 and K_z^rho={x:dist(x,boundary K_z)>=rho}. Set
B=max_(K_z) U+max_(K_z) L. On the rho/2 interior core the difference U-L
is Lipschitz with constant at most 2B/rho. Indeed each nonnegative concave
summand has oscillation at most its maximum, and restriction to line segments
of length at least rho/2 in either direction bounds every directional slope.
If A=|U(x)-L(x)| at x in K_z^rho, the ball of radius A rho/(4B) lies in the
rho/2 core and has |U-L|>=A/2. Thus, with omega_d the unit d-ball volume,

    sup_(K_z^rho)|U-L|
      <= [2*4^d B^d integral_(K_z)|U-L|
                            /(omega_d rho^d)]^(1/(d+1)).        (9)

For delta in a fixed bounded interval, (6), (8), and (9) give an explicit
O(delta^(1/[2(d+1)])) interior modulus. This is not asserted to be optimal.

There is a real boundary limitation. Take one interval K=[0,1], L=1, source
Y=1/2, sigma=1, and rho uniform. For 0<e<1/2 set

    H_e(x)=min(1, 1/2+x/(2e)),
    U_e(x)=exp[e(1-log 2)] H_e(x).

These are positive continuous concave functions, and

    integral_0^1 log H_e=e(log 2-1),
    integral_0^1 log U_e=0,
    U_e(1/2)=exp(delta_e),  delta_e=e(1-log 2)->0.

Nevertheless U_e(0)->1/2 while L(0)=1. On every compact subset of (0,1]
there is uniform convergence to one. The corresponding energy-weighted
buffers converge uniformly because interval energy vanishes at the endpoints.
This is a near-certificate example, not a claim about exact moving-body
optimizers. It shows why (9) cannot simply be extended to the boundary.

## 4. Moving-body theorem and its hypotheses

Let actual compatible families K_(m,z) on the SAME finite base P converge
fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to K_z. Every limit fiber is positive and
full-dimensional. Hence, for all sufficiently large m, the families have
uniform boundedness, positive volume bounds, and common interior balls in each
fiber. Let C_m be their canonical hulls, M_m their actual masses, and Sigma_m
the actual within-fiber covariance matrices divided by M_m. Then
M_m->M and Sigma_m->Sigma, with Sigma positive definite.

Fix epsilon>0. For a parameter U on C_m define the actual buffered depth by
including all pure-base closed halfspaces, and, for every nonzero continuous
normal u and arbitrary base tilt a, the closed cap

    a.(Z-p)+u.(X-y)
       >= -epsilon [U(p,y) E_(K_(m,p))(y)/M_m]^(1/N)
                    sqrt(u^T Sigma_m u).                        (10)

Let Q_m(U) be its maximum over the actual integer-fiber set S_m. The definition
of pure-base caps is unchanged as a set of finite base subsets, but their
weights are the current volumes V_(m,z). Normalize every U by
M_m^(-1) integral_(S_m) log U=0.

Assume the fixed L and certificate (1) have the following actual-depth
property: every Y_i is a deepest mark for the limiting family and L, their
common raw depth is Q, and

    Q < b_base(p_i) for every i.                     (11)

Thus y_i is interior and the scalar-buffer strictness theorem applies. the contributor's
certificate proves that L is a global fixed-body parameter optimizer.

Let U_m be positive continuous concave normalized parameters on C_m such that

    Q_m(U_m) <= inf_U Q_m(U)+o(1),                    (12)

where the infimum uses the same positive continuous concave normalized class.
Exact minimizers are a special case; their existence is not assumed or proved
here. Then:

(a) U_m converges to L uniformly on every compact subset of the interior of
    each limiting sampled fiber (evaluating at the same continuous coordinates,
    which belong to the approximating fiber for large m).
(b) Their zero-extended sampled restrictions converge in mixed L1; likewise
    their zero-extended logarithms converge in mixed L1.
(c) Their actual buffers, extended by zero outside each fiber, converge uniformly
    on the finite union of fiber coordinate spaces.
(d) Q_m(U_m)->Q and Q_m(U_m)/M_m->Q/M.

There is no hypothesis about convergence of U_m between sampled fibers. There
is no differentiability or cap-regularity assumption. The proof follows.

## 5. A legal reference competitor and the depth upper bound

The canonical hull C has a relative ambient ball B(O,r) in its interior.
Since C_m->C, write e_m=d_H(C_m,C). The affine homothety

    H_m(w)=O+lambda_m(w-O),  lambda_m=r/(r+e_m)

maps C_m into C: the support inequality uses
lambda_m e_m<=(1-lambda_m)r in every relative ambient direction. Therefore
L(H_m(w)) is a positive continuous concave parameter on C_m. Its mixed
log-normalizing factor tends to one, since L has a positive lower bound and
is uniformly continuous on C, and the actual sampled measures converge in
total variation. Let L_m be this normalized competitor.

This is only a way of defining a parameter on C_m. It is NOT a transformation
of the mixed body or its lattice bases; no depth invariance under H_m is used.
On sampled points converging to w in S, L_m converges to L(w).

Joint marked-energy continuity, covariance convergence, and the all-direction
slab estimate give Q_m(L_m)->Q. To recall why unbounded base tilts cause no
problem, normalize ||u||=1. At a fixed base p the change of threshold between
converging marks is bounded by

    |y_m-y| + epsilon sup_(||u||=1)|f_m(p,y_m)G_m(u)-f(p,y)G(u)|.

It contains no base tilt a. A common bounded region bounds the mass in every
such continuous slab uniformly. Pure-base caps select exactly the same finite
base subset and change mass by at most the total fiber symmetric difference.
Taking infima, then maxima over the finite compact fibers, proves the claim,
including closed pure-base boundaries. By (12),

    Q_m(U_m)<=Q+o(1).                                 (13)

## 6. Push the old certificate into the new actual fibers

Choose g_z=centroid(K_z); any fixed uniformly interior points would suffice.
There exist common numbers t_m>=0 tending to zero, t_m<1, such that

    T_m(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-t_m)(X-g_z)),
    I_(m,z):=T_m K_z subset K_(m,z).                  (14)

For example, if B(g_z,r_z) subset K_z and the fiber Hausdorff error is e_m',
the support inequalities imply (14) whenever t_m min_z r_z>=e_m'.

Push each old row rho_i by T_m. Its full barycenter is

    Y_i^m=(p_i,(1-t_m)y_i+t_m b_i),
    b_i=E_(rho_i) g_Z.                                (15)

In particular its base is exactly the same integer p_i. Since the pushed row
is supported on S_m and C_m is its actual convex hull, Y_i^m belongs to the
fiber K_(m,p_i). It tends to the interior point Y_i.

T_m need not be affine in the base coordinate, and no affine centroid graph is
assumed. This map is applied ONLY to the certificate rows, not to produce a
new convex family or to assert an invariance of cap geometry.

At a fixed old mark Y_i, increasing its scalar parameter value from L_i to any
s>L_i strictly raises its depth above Q. This is precisely the proper-gap
strictness in the contributor's theorem: if the new depth is still below atomic depth,
choose an attained new minimizing cap. Its own trace is proper, so lowering
the buffer removes a positive own-fiber strip. If the new depth reaches atomic
depth, (11) already supplies the strict inequality.

For fixed s>L_i, the scalar depth at (Y_i^m,s) converges to the scalar depth at
(Y_i,s) by the same all-direction estimate, without using U_m. Monotonicity
in the scalar parameter and (13) consequently imply

    eta_m:=max_i [log(U_m(Y_i^m)/L_i)]_+ ->0.           (16)

Jensen for the ACTUAL concave U_m and the pushed rows now gives

    b_m:=E_(P_0)[U_m(T_m w)/L(w)]
        =sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) E_(rho_i) U_m(T_m w)
        <=sum_i sigma_i U_m(Y_i^m)/L_i
        <=exp(eta_m).                                 (17)

This estimate does not require any uniform lower bound or initial compactness
of U_m. It is the step that controls a possibly varying concave parameter.

## 7. Uniform sampled bounds and logarithmic collars

There are s_m>=0 tending to zero with

    K_(m,z) subset g_z+(1+s_m)(K_z-g_z)

for all z. Thus I_(m,z) contains the homothetic image

    g_z+q_m(K_(m,z)-g_z),  q_m=(1-t_m)/(1+s_m)->1.

Positivity and concavity imply
max_(K_(m,z)) U_m <=q_m^(-1) max_(I_(m,z)) U_m. Applying (7) to I_(m,z),
then changing variables by (14), yields

    max_(K_(m,z)) U_m
       <= (d+1)/(q_m V_z) integral_(K_z) U_m(T_m(z,X)) dX
       <= (d+1) M L_max exp(eta_m)/(q_m V_z).           (18)

Hence all sampled maxima are bounded above by one finite B, chosen >=1.
Their lower bounds follow from normalization. Writing m_(m,z)=max U_m on
that fiber and w_(m,z)=V_(m,z)/M_m, we have

    0=sum_z w_(m,z) average_(K_(m,z)) log U_m
      <=w_(m,z)log m_(m,z)+(1-w_(m,z))log B.

All w_(m,z) are bounded below, so m_(m,z)>=c>0 uniformly.

These upper and lower bounds give uniform integrability of log U_m directly.
Indeed the first part of (7) gives

    |{U_m<s m_(m,z)}| <=[1-(1-s)^d]V_(m,z)<=d s V_(m,z).

Consequently, for small r>0,

    integral_{U_m<r} |log U_m|
        <=C r(1+|log r|),                             (19)

uniformly over all sampled fibers. On any measurable set of volume h tending
to zero, splitting at r proportional to h gives a bound
C h(1+|log h|) for the absolute logarithmic integral. Positive logarithms are
bounded by log B. In particular the vanishing collars
K_(m,z) outside I_(m,z) have total absolute log integral tending to zero.

## 8. Pulled-back entropy, interior convergence, and actual depths

Set R_m(w)=U_m(T_m w)/L(w). The Jacobian of T_m on EVERY fiber is the same
number j_m=(1-t_m)^d. Since U_m is normalized on S_m and L on S,

    xi_m:=E_(P_0) log R_m
       = -1/(M j_m) sum_z
                     integral_(K_(m,z) outside I_(m,z)) log U_m dX
       ->0.                                          (20)

The common contraction factor is why there is no unaccounted fiber-dependent
Jacobian in this formula. If h_m is the total collar volume, (19) gives
|xi_m|<=C h_m(1+|log h_m|) for small positive h_m.

By log Jensen and (17), exp(xi_m)<=b_m<=exp(eta_m). The probability law
(R_m/b_m)P_0 therefore satisfies

    KL(P_0 || (R_m/b_m)P_0)=log b_m-xi_m.

Pinsker gives, for example, the explicit sufficient bound

    E_(P_0)|R_m-1|
       <=exp(eta_m)sqrt(2(eta_m+|xi_m|))
          +exp(eta_m)-1+|exp(xi_m)-1| ->0.             (21)

Thus U_m composed with T_m tends to L in mixed L1. Its restriction to each
old fiber is concave and uniformly bounded by (18). The interior estimate (9)
applies and proves locally uniform convergence there. Uniform interior
Lipschitz bounds for U_m on the approximating fibers, together with T_m->id,
then give convergence at the SAME continuous coordinates on each old fiber
core. This proves (a).

Uniform bounds and the small volumes of outer/inner boundary layers upgrade
this to mixed L1 convergence of zero-extended functions. Interior positivity
of L gives logarithmic convergence on cores; (19) treats the remaining sets.
This proves (b). Here 'zero extension of log U_m' means the function equal to
log U_m inside its fiber and zero outside, not the logarithm of the zero
extension of U_m.

Joint energy continuity now proves (c). In detail, on compact fiber interiors
use (a). At sequences tending to a fiber boundary the energies tend uniformly
to zero, while (18) bounds U_m, so

    [U_m E_(K_(m,z))/M_m]^(1/N) -> [L E_(K_z)/M]^(1/N)

uniformly with zero extensions. The covariance factors also converge. Apply
the all-direction slab comparison from Section 5 to obtain uniform marked
buffered-depth convergence and convergence of its maximum. Alternatively
(13) gives the upper bound, and evaluating any Y_i^m, where (a) applies and
the actual scalar depth tends to Q, gives the lower bound. This proves (d).

## 9. What the theorem does and does not add

The root certificate already establishes exact fixed-body parameter optimality.
The new conclusions are a quantitative entropy-to-interior modulus and a
nonregular stability theorem for optimizing parameters as the ACTUAL bodies
vary. The row-push construction supplies the missing comparison across changing
domains while preserving every source integer base. It does not require an
affine selection from the fibers or a uniform-fiber lift of a volume row.

The fixed-body boundary example prevents a gratuitous stronger topology.
No derivative of the optimized value, body-neutral path, interchange of
minimax quantifiers, or Gamma payment follows. A separate geometric argument
is still needed to improve a joint body/parameter minimum.
